news.title: Defender named Star of the Match in Man City win!
news.body_en: There were several outstanding candidates for Star of the Match in Chelsea’s crucial Women’s Super League victory over Manchester City, and Blues fans have voted for their winner. The poll on the Chelsea Official App proved to be one of the closest of the campaign, highlighting just how impressive Sonia Bompastor’s side were across the pitch as Sandy Baltimore’s first-half goal secured the points. Baltimore finished second in our poll with 30 per cent of the vote, as her spectacular strike fired the Blues to the top of the table. Lucy Bronze came in third place, with 26 per cent of the vote, following another tireless display at the back. That meant the winner of our poll, just edging out Baltimore and Bronze, was Veerle Buurman. The young defender picked up 37 per cent of the votes cast after being introduced unexpectedly early following an injury to Kadeisha Buchanan. Buurman produced a defensive masterclass and maturity beyond her years to help us keep a potent Man City attack quiet and register a well-earned clean sheet.

news.title: OTD: West Brom 0-3 Chelsea | 15 November 2008
1996/97 remembered - part three: The signing of Gianfranco Zola
news.body_en: We continue celebrating Chelsea’s legendary 1996/97 campaign 30 years on by telling the story of Gianfranco Zola’s acquisition, and his subsequent rise to become one of our greatest ever players. We have previously focused on the thrilling summer of ’96 and the tragic death of Matthew Harding. Now we recount Zola's signing - 30 years ago this month - through our archive of first-hand interviews, with words from the very people who had the privilege of witnessing a truly great Premier League import up close. Chelsea's 1996/97 campaign had got off to a decent start under Ruud Gullit's management. Six wins, four draws, and only two defeats suggested the Blues were becoming harder to beat, and perhaps even consistent enough to start challenging at the very top of the table. The signs were good, and things were about to get even better, as Chelsea's club historian, Rick Glanvill, recalls. Glanvill: ‘The Chelsea of 96/97 had Di Matteo dominating midfield and Leboeuf spraying the ball from the back. You had Frode Grodas, the Norwegian goalkeeper who'd come in on a free, who was pretty solid and unspectacular. 'You had Mark Hughes and Gianluca Vialli up front. You had Dennis Wise. I've never seen a player adapt so well over the course of his career to all the different circumstances, and he really was the ringmaster. So you had a really good spine. But what it needed was a maestro, and actually, that's what we got.’ Zola made his name at Napoli in Serie A, first as Diego Maradona's understudy, and later his successor. It was quite a schooling for Zola. The man many consider the greatest player of all time took the Italian under his wing, helping him make the most of his exceptional skill despite his lack of height, teaching him set-piece techniques and, on one occasion, even letting him start in his beloved No.10 shirt. ‘It was the most beautiful thing I could ever imagine,’ Zola later said. In '93, Zola left for Parma and helped a star-studded team reach the Cup Winners' Cup final a year later, and then win the UEFA Cup in '95. Gianluca Vialli was on the losing Juventus side, while Zola was named in the inaugural European Team of the Year. Though his goal-to-game ratio at Parma was excellent, and earned him a place in Italy's Euro '96 team – where he famously had a penalty saved in the final group game against Germany, which stopped the Azzurri advancing to the knockout stage – he wasn't chosen to lead the attack by incoming Parma manager Carlo Ancelotti. The future Chelsea boss preferred a 4-4-2 formation, with new signings Hernan Crespo and Enrico Chiesa up front. Zola was shunted out to the wing. The situation reached a boiling point when Mario Stanic, another future Blue then at Club Bruges, was pictured in the stands at a game, expected to sign imminently and take Zola's place in the team. It paved the way for his move to London, and it provided everyone at the club with a much-needed pick-me-up a fortnight or so after Matthew Harding's tragic death. Zola: ‘I certainly came with a lot of willingness to do well. I knew I was going through a difficult moment in Parma, and I came here with a determination to do good, and to prove that it was just a bad spell of my career. 'I was really lucky to find a fantastic atmosphere at the club. My team-mates were unbelievable. Plus the crowd, from the first day was fantastic, really. They made my life very easy. All that came on the pitch was a consequence of what I found outside it.’ ‘I think it was a mistake,’ Ancelotti later admitted. ‘It was my first experience in Serie A, and I was not able to change the system. He probably would not have gone to Chelsea if I had done.’ Thank goodness Ancelotti didn't. Chelsea had declined to sign Zola for £10 million a year earlier, but the Bosman ruling meant his value was depreciating day by day, and so player-manager Ruud Gullit and the club jumped at the chance to acquire his services for £4.5m, as then-managing director Colin Hutchinson recalled. Hutchinson: ‘I'd been on his trail for 18 months. Glenn [Hoddle] loved him. He didn't have an agent. He was represented by a solicitor, and I built up a good relationship with him. I got wind from Parma that he was available, and two agents representing Parma came to England. ‘They visited Tottenham. They visited Chelsea. I discussed a deal with them over two days. They couldn't finalise it because it was down to the president. I'd made contact by then with the guy who I already knew, his lawyer. And that night I flew to Parma, met the president that evening, and thrashed out a deal. ‘The next morning I met Zola and his representative. We had four hours of talks. He was obviously, for the sake of his family, a little bit concerned about upping sticks and moving to England, but by late in the afternoon, he signed the deal before Tottenham ever got out of the starting blocks.’ Italian TV were the first to break the news on the Friday afternoon, before terms were officially agreed between the clubs. The signing was completed later that day, the night of 8 November 1996. Zola was introduced to the British public on the Monday at a well-attended Stamford Bridge press conference. He spoke basic English, but he could explain why he had decided to move to Stamford Bridge. ‘Because Chelsea believes in me,’ he said. He signed a three-and-a-half-year deal worth a reported £25,000 a week. Zola: ‘The impression was good because when I came over here, Di Matteo and Luca Vialli were already playing for Chelsea, so they informed me about the situation. They spoke very highly about the club. ‘Obviously, it was quite different from Italy. In those days, Italy was huge on football, so there were little differences. In Italy, everything was taken to an extreme. The preparation was to an extreme. All the aspects of the game, they were all very much looked after. In my opinion, too much. I believe it was losing the fun part of it. ‘At the end of the day, for footballers – no matter how big you are or how much you earn – what is important for them is to have fun for what they're doing. At least that was what I was feeling. In that moment in Italy, the game was so big, so important, so high level that it was losing something.’ Zola's arrival prompted some speculation that Mark Hughes might leave, with the futures of other attack-minded players John Spencer, Mark Stein and Gavin Peacock also thrown into the air. Spencer left for QPR for £2.5m ten days after Zola's arrival, with Stein and Peacock soon leaving on loan to Stoke and QPR respectively. Gullit: ‘I was trying to look for something that would suit my team. We had this good opportunity to get Zola, and that was the icing on the cake. I didn't have to think about it. When this opportunity came, I said immediately: "Yes, get this man," because I knew how good he was.’ And so, very quickly, did his new teammates. Zola instantly shone in training, including in a game against the reserves a couple of days before his Chelsea debut at Blackburn Rovers. They were archetypal Premiership opponent in those days. Zola: ‘It was difficult for me. I was playing in midfield, and I couldn't get the ball, actually! It was always flying above my head. That was very unusual, because the game was very fast, and obviously very physical. What I remember is that I felt good, but I couldn't get the ball enough in order to make a difference. ‘It was still a moment in which I was understanding how the game was, and it was very useful. There is a great picture (below) that I still have in my house. It says: "Welcome to the English game, Zola." And you can see me upside down. You see the feet where my head should be, and the head where the feet should be!’ He got an assist for Gianluca Vialli on his home debut against high-flying Newcastle United, a 1-1 draw, and their manager, Kevin Keegan, remarked afterwards that Zola was a bundle of tricks and a tremendous addition to the Premier League. He scored his first goal in his next game at Stamford Bridge, against Everton, with a free-kick Blues fans would quickly learn was his trademark. Zola: ‘I remember free-kicks were something that I practised a lot, and it was a good goal.’ It was the first of 14 free-kicks Zola netted for Chelsea. But it wasn't all rosy. Three draws and two defeats in the five games after Zola's arrival had some questioning the value of his signing. Was the league too quick and physical for him? At just 5ft 6in, would he struggle to impact games? Was he, as some speculated, just another foreign mercenary looking to pick up a final pay packet in the increasingly wealthy Premier League? In 10 seconds of football, Zola answered any lingering doubts surrounding his effectiveness. West Ham United were the last visitors to Stamford Bridge before Christmas, when Zola twisted and turned their hardman defender Julian Dicks inside and out before firing into the net. It was an awe-inspiring goal that showed Zola could deliver in the Premier League. Zola: ‘I remember we played very well. Not only the goal – it was a good goal and there were some good goals from also the other players – but we played a good game and the partnership was working very well. From that moment, I believe Ruud didn’t change anymore. ‘It was good for me as well because in that game, I really played well. I felt like everything that came to my mind, I was able to do. Although I didn’t realise how dangerous it was to do what I did to Julian!’ ‘Everybody loves him,’ said Gullit afterwards. ‘I think he stole their hearts, and I'm very happy for him. He already played very well in a couple of games, but he was frustrated by the fact that we couldn't win. Now he’s very happy, he’s doing well and it’s also a good thing for the Premier League.’ That day was not only significant for the dazzling solo goal Zola scored. It was also when his partnership with Mark Hughes up front was born. Vialli was injured, so Zola moved forward from the position where he began his Chelsea career, in midfield. Zola: ‘Ruud said that probably midfield was the best position for me because he was afraid that playing me up front, I couldn't get any space, plus I would be under strict and close marking. He said: ‘Probably they will hit you, they will kick you, you’re not going to find space, so I prefer to play you in midfield.’ ‘Then Luca got injured, so he had to play me up front, and we found this perfect partnership with Mark. From that moment, the team started to get results with consistency, and it didn’t change anymore.’ ‘Mark was really important to me because he made my game easy. He all the time was creating space for me and for the others. 'When you have somebody like him up front, it becomes easy. He's one of those players that they can play in different generations, and they're going to be up to date all the time. They are so intelligent, so strong, determined, that they're always useful.’ Glanvill: ‘Partnerships are so underrated in football, and you could immediately see that Mark Hughes thought: “My goodness, what have I got next to me now?”’ Hughes: ‘Franco was a joy to play with. He's one of the special players of that era. It was a good mix. I was there to be a little bit of a battering ram, and I would say with smaller stature players, they have to be really exceptional to make an impact at the highest level. That's why Franco was so good: he was able to affect almost every game he played in. ‘I played a part, maybe, bashing holes in the defence. He used to exploit that, but you've still got to be good enough to recognise situations if they present themselves. It was easy to play with Franco. ‘He was an easy target, because it was more aggressive in those days. It was refereed in a different way. There was more leniency, and you had the opportunity to stop good teams playing by being aggressive. 'That’s what teams used to try and do, but he was a strong little guy. He was always in the gym, and in fairness, when he was stripped off, he was cut, so he'd worked hard. You could see he'd been in the gym to try and make himself stronger. So good guy, great pro, great player.’ Gullit: ‘I had a conflict of who was going to be playing because I had Gianluca there and I had Mark Hughes. He was vital for us. It worked straight away. I knew exactly the formation because Mark Hughes was the one who was strong, could hold the ball, and Zola could play around him. He could do all the things he needed to do. ‘They were great. It was just the partnership you always look for in a team. One very unselfish player who could block the ball, hold the ball for the rest to become better. Then the other player who has his fantasy and also has his ability to score incredible goals.’ Zola was soon completely settled, even if there were some things he would never quite get used to. Zola: ‘It was unusual to spend Christmas playing football because normally you have a break during that time. But I enjoyed it, I really enjoyed it. Although I didn't enjoy the party when I went to a disco with my team-mates, and Grodas nearly killed me because I wasn't drinking a huge bottle of vodka! ‘That first year was something really special. I found the perfect atmosphere to play well and also to behave well. I liked the mentality, I liked the philosophy of the people, of the way they play the game and the way they support the game. I was in perfect symphony with them. ‘I found the perfect environment for me. The way I see football is the same as people live and see football over here. So I didn't have to change at all. I just had to relax and play my best football as I always thought it should be.’ It was not just Zola's extraordinary ability that Blues fans, and indeed supporters of other clubs, were warming to. His personality was starting to shine through. The commentator Martin Tyler remembers his career and what it was like dealing with him from a journalist's perspective. Tyler: ‘Well, what a signing. What a wonderful guy, which we didn’t really know at the time. He had class on the pitch, and charm off it. ‘Suddenly this was becoming, from the media point of view, a different dynamic really, dealing with players whose English wasn't their first language. Could he speak English? Will we get anything? Would he do anything? ‘He'd come out of Sardinia, where I think he'd learned to stand his ground, and being in the Maradona world as well, at Napoli, so we knew about him. Maradona was a bit chunkier than Franco, but you can't play at that level in that kind of environment without having some resilience as well as wonderful skill. ‘He was absolutely charming as a guy, which I think probably helped. He was so modest about doing the most sublime things on the field, and just a joy to be around.’ Zola's honesty and humility are two of the most fondly recalled characteristics. His dedication also burns bright in the memories of those who had the good fortune of playing with him or watching him firsthand. A very young John Terry was one such man. Terry: ‘When he came in, he was such a big name in the world of football, and he really took to the younger players. I was 16 at the time doing my YTS, but he had so much time for everyone around the football club, including the younger players, wanting to help us, wanting to always advise us. ‘His professionalism was amazing, just watching the way he prepared for training, after training, for games. As a kid, I used to have to be in at half seven, eight o'clock. He'd come in at eight o'clock most mornings, do gym and strength work, which back then was kind of unheard of. He was way ahead of his time in that way. ‘We’d pick his brains and ask him questions: “Well, what are you doing? Why are you doing it?" He formed a little head tennis court in the gym. He got the tape out, with this little ball, and he used to beat us all every morning. ‘He took care in everything. He didn't accept people not working hard, not trying. When you've got players like that around as well, it naturally brings the group and the intensity up – and the quality for sure. ‘After training he'd grab a bag of balls, and he'd do one-on-ones. He'd call you over as a young defender, run at you and twist and turn and have you in tangles. What a learning curve. He would step in and say: "Right, you need to position your body this way to make it more difficult for the striker." ‘He was always advising, always practising his free-kicks. Over the years we've seen so many go in the top corner. As a young player you’d be sitting in the stands, and every time he got a free-kick outside the box, you fancied him to score. It wasn’t because he would randomly get one in. It’s because he worked hard and practised on it. That was a great lesson and example for all of us. ‘It was a nightmare training against him because he could do everything. He could drop off, he could play behind. Play in that little hole, twist and turn, but he was quick over five, ten yards, probably one of the quickest at the club. He worked on his explosiveness. He could win headers. And his natural football ability was one of the best I’ve ever seen. ‘As a centre-half, did you go tight? He had the quality and the brain to spin and go in behind, and the acceleration to pull away as well. He gave us so many great memories, and what a real true legend at the football club. ‘He always had time for the fans after games, and always stressed to us younger players to make sure you always give time to the supporters because one day they’ll really want your autograph. Little things like that will stick with me forever.’ Defender Frank Sinclair and fitness coach Ade Mafe remember what it was like working with him. Mafe: ‘He came in and was hardworking. He would always stay after training and do his free-kicks. He bought himself one of the first portable free-kick walls I'd ever seen. He would always come out after training and be practising and be practising and be practising. ‘He was very big into stretching, yoga. He was very big into strength training. He would challenge me to 10-metre runs from starts. He was a complete professional, a physically great specimen. His dedication to his training and the dedication to his football are the reasons why he reaped the rewards of actually playing.’ Sinclair: ‘He improved me. He was one of the first players that I saw with my own eyes staying on the training pitch and working at stuff. Regardless of how good he was, he wanted to improve. ‘I stayed out a lot with him because we used to do drills, just me and him, where he'd be attacking me defending and just have a goalkeeper in there, and he was just trying to get half a yard to get shots off, and he liked doing it with me obviously because of my physical attributes and my pace would make it difficult for him to do that. ‘We spent many hours on the training pitch after sessions had finished just working on stuff like that through my career, which I believe improved me as a defender as well.’ That was an opinion Steve Clarke, a fellow defender, shared. Clarke: ‘Training was always difficult because you couldn't kick him because you knew you needed him on the Saturday! He made you a better defender because he kept you on your toes all the time in training, and his performances when he came to us that season were absolutely outstanding, and he probably just upped the ante at the club a little bit. ‘The club brought even more quality into the group and helped to make us as successful as we were. Tremendous man, very humble, a great person first and foremost, and then on top of that, he's an absolutely gifted footballer. To work day in, day out with Gianfranco was just a privilege.’ Dan Petrescu, another key member of Chelsea’s cosmopolitan squad, rated him extremely highly. Petrescu: ‘He made a big impact. I remember the goal against Everton he scored, and all the fans were thinking: "God, who is this guy?" And the professionalism he brought to the club as well because the young players could see Zola at the training ground, and we saw Zola at the training ground, the way he trained. He stayed after training; he stayed in the gym. Zola was a great player; maybe the greatest I played with.’ By the end of his first full month in English football, Zola's hard work on and off the pitch was well and truly paying off. He netted a Boxing Day brace at Aston Villa and followed it two days later with another strike, this one against Sheffield Wednesday. That meant he finished December with five goals, so it was no surprise when he was subsequently voted the Premiership's Player of the Month. The memorable moments kept on coming. Late in January '97, Zola brilliantly equalised in the epic FA Cup fourth round game against Liverpool that will be covered in the next long read on our 1996/97 campaign. That goal displayed the venom with which he could hit a football as well as the outstanding ability of his supposedly weaker left foot. An even more special strike followed a few weeks later, two minutes into the home fixture against Manchester United. Taking a Dan Petrescu pass in the inside right channel, Zola cut inside Denis Irwin, who was left to slide off the pitch towards the redeveloping Shed End. Another grizzled top-flight defender, Gary Pallister, now stood between Zola and the goal. Two touches and a drop of the shoulder later, and Zola had glided past him into a central position on the cusp of the six-yard box. He shot early and low on his left. The considerable frame of Peter Schmeichel didn't even move. It was a goal that perhaps more than any other Zola scored epitomised the innumerable qualities he possessed: the touch, the skill, the awareness, the bravery in taking on players much bigger than him, the adeptness with both feet, the finishing ability, the confidence. Blues fans would never grow tired of watching him, including season ticket holder and renowned DJ Trevor Nelson. Nelson: ‘I thought [Glenn] Hoddle was good. I thought Ruud [Gullit] was good. I knew Zola was good, but I couldn’t believe what we got. He was the spark to everything we did. You just wanted to get the ball to Zola. Something magical would happen. We felt like he was a genius.’ Alex Ferguson was a long-term fan of Zola's. The striker proved a constant thorn in the Manchester United defence from the moment he scored that sensational goal two minutes into his first ever game against them. ‘He annoyed me,’ Ferguson said a decade later. ‘He was one of those players who was unperturbed about who he was playing against. You always saw a smile on his face, and that annoyed me. I said: “How can he be enjoying himself playing against United? Nobody else does.”’ The benefit on those around Zola was increasingly evident. Glanvill: ‘You have a team where all the different parts are working quite well, but it takes one element that's added and everything is raised completely, and that's what you found when Gianfranco Zola came in. ‘All of a sudden, Dan Petrescu felt much more important in the way things were working. You'd see players like an Eddie Newton, for example, would do his typical Eddie spin, give the ball to Franco, and then magic would happen. You just saw the whole team grow to meet the excellence of Zola.’ Such was Zola and Hughes' form up front, Gianluca Vialli was not able to win his place back in 96/97. Vialli had honestly admitted that Zola made him look ordinary. ‘Of all the Italian players to come here, I have the feeling he will be the best,’ Vialli said when Zola joined. He wasn't wrong. Indeed, such was Zola's impact in his first season that at its end he was voted the Football Writers' Association Footballer of the Year. He received the award from Stanley Matthews, the inaugural winner half a century earlier, a couple of days before the FA Cup final. Zola: ‘We didn't have anything like that in Italy. When I was awarded it, I was over the moon. It was so many famous players and talented players that came before me, and I was so happy to receive it from Mr Stanley Matthews. It was something special really. It was one of those moments that you will remember forever.’ Glanvill: ‘He wasn't just a brilliant player for Chelsea. He was the best player in the Premier League, and it had been so long since you could say that about a Chelsea player. Really, you're almost going back to Ray Wilkins being the best in the top flight. That's how much he elevated Chelsea, that all of a sudden people liked our club because Zola played for us, and they loved Zola.’ Six years after the '97 Cup final win, Zola left Chelsea to join Cagliari in his native Sardinia. In total, he made 312 appearances for the club, scoring 80 goals, so many of them unforgettable. He picked up winner's medals in the FA Cup twice, the Cup Winners' Cup, when he scored the only goal in the final in Stockholm, the League Cup, and the Super Cup. Zola's exceptional ability on the pitch and his wonderful personality off it mean there's no question he will forever go down as one of the greatest ever players to pull on the blue shirt. Zola: ‘I, and all the others, enjoyed it very much because there was a lot of enthusiasm, there was a great atmosphere, not only around the stadium, but also with the players. 'It was really good, and that was one of the main reasons why we were successful. We were allowed to get into the system very quickly. There was a collaboration from everyone for us to be successful, and that was very important.’ In the fourth long read retelling the story of the 1996/97 season, we will remember the epic 4-2 FA Cup win over Liverpool…

news.title: Internationals: Neto and Estevao feature while Ezenwata scores for Young Lions
news.body_en: Pedro Neto, Estevao Willian and a selection of young Blues were all involved in another action-packed day of international action. Neto started for Portugal in their 4-1 defeat to Denmark in the UEFA Nations League, with fellow Blue Geovany Quenda an unused substitute for the hosts. Chelsea goalkeeper Filip Jorgensen was also named among the substitutes for Denmark. Our winger was replaced with just under half an hour remaining, as Portugal suffered their first defeat of the campaign. Despite the result, they remain top of League A Group 4, three points ahead of the Danes. Elsewhere in the Nations League, Genesis Antwi was an unused substitute as Sweden secured a 3-2 victory over Bosnia and Herzegovina. The Swedes are now five points clear at the top of League B Group 4. Meanwhile, Estevao started for Brazil in their 3-2 defeat to Japan in Singapore. Japan raced into a 2-0 lead through Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura before Vinicius Junior pulled one back for Brazil. Estevao came close to finding the net, but was denied by Japan goalkeeper Zion Suzuki. The Blues winger was replaced by Alisson Santana shortly before the hour mark, and Vinicius struck again in the 75th minute to bring Brazil level. However, Japan had the final say as Tatsuhiro Sakamoto scored a dramatic stoppage-time winner, securing his country's second victory over Brazil. At youth level, England's Under-18s suffered a 3-0 defeat to Sweden in their second fixture of the November international window. Five Chelsea representatives featured in the contest, with Calvin Diakite, Ryan Kavuma-McQueen and Riley Ebho all starting, while Jashayde Greenwood and Gabriel Sambou were introduced from the bench. There was better news for England's Under-19s, who made it two wins from two with an emphatic 5-0 victory over Belarus in UEFA European Under-19 Championship qualifying. Chelsea forward Chizaram Ezenwata was among the goalscorers, converting a penalty to score the Young Lions' fourth of the afternoon. Fellow Blues Freddy Bernal, Landon Emenalo and Reggie Walsh were also involved, with all three starting the contest. England's Under-17s also continued their impressive qualifying campaign with a 2-0 victory over Poland. Chelsea trio Reggie Watson, Josh Henry and Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli were all named in the starting line-up as the Young Lions secured their second consecutive win in UEFA European Under-17 Championship qualifying.

news.title: WSL Full Match: Chelsea vs Manchester City
Sonia Bompastor provides injury update on Kadeisha Buchanan and Melvine Malard
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor has provided an update on the fitness of Kadeisha Buchanan and Melvine Malard after both Chelsea players were forced off with injuries during our 1-0 victory over Manchester City. The Blues secured a huge three points at Stamford Bridge, with Sandy Baltimore's stunning strike on the stroke of half-time moving us above City and into the top spot in the Women's Super League. However, there was concern for Chelsea as Buchanan was forced off after just 12 minutes, with Veerle Buurman coming on to replace the defender. Malard also had to be withdrawn before half-time, making way for Aggie Beever-Jones in the 35th minute. Bompastor explained that Buchanan had taken a knock during training on Friday and that she felt the defender was not herself from the beginning of the match. Sonia explained further: 'With Kadeisha Buchanan, she took a knock in training yesterday on her head, and I just felt from the beginning of the game she was not herself, so probably off the back of what happened in training. I was also almost forced to do that one.' The Chelsea head coach also confirmed that Malard had felt something in her hamstring, prompting her early withdrawal. Bompastor added: 'With Melvine, I was forced to do the substitution because she felt her hamstring, so we will assess her tomorrow and see how she is.'

news.title: WSL Highlights: Chelsea 1-0 Manchester City
Gallery: Baltimore's screamer fires Blues to top of the WSL!
'It's a great feeling to be top of the table'
'It's nice that we kept a clean sheet'
Sonia Bompastor praises Chelsea character after Man City victory
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor praised her players' character and defensive performance after Chelsea beat Manchester City 1-0 at Stamford Bridge to move to the top of the Women's Super League. Sandy Baltimore's stunning strike on the stroke of half-time proved decisive, as the Blues claimed a huge three points against our title rivals and ended City's unbeaten start to the season. The victory was particularly important after Chelsea dropped points in the league against Everton last weekend and suffered a Champions League stalemate against BK Hacken during the week. Bompastor was delighted with the response from her players, highlighting the hard work and determination required to keep a dangerous City attack at bay. 'I am happy. Credit to my players. We showed a lot of character coming into the game today. It was not easy, especially on the back of the points we dropped in the league last weekend and in the Champions League,' the Chelsea head coach said. 'The players worked really hard, and the performance was a good one. Especially not to concede a goal against this side, Manchester City, so I think it was a strong defensive performance.' One of the standout performers was young defender Veerle Buurman, who came on after just 12 minutes following an injury to Kadeisha Buchanan. She helped keep City's leading scorer Khadija Shaw quiet throughout the contest. Bompastor was particularly pleased with the way the team dealt with the striker, while also praising Buurman's individual contribution. 'You know, when you come into this game, you try to keep her [Shaw] quiet as much as possible. When it is the case at the beginning of the game, that is good, but you have to do it for the whole game and the 90-plus minutes,' she explained. 'I felt Veerle Buurman had an exceptional game. Being young but being able not to let her have a lot of opportunities was a strong performance, but the whole team had a really strong performance in terms of the defensive aspect.' Bompastor was also asked about Katie McCabe's message to the team to 'play like dogs' before the game, and was happy with whatever approach helped her players deliver on the pitch. 'If that makes them good and happy, then I'm happy for them to play like dogs or cats or whatever they want,' she added. 'We have shown this season that we are doing well in not being easy to break down, and today was another opportunity to show that. To do that against the top teams is a nice feeling.'

news.title: Lucy Bronze on Chelsea's consistency against 'top' Manchester City
news.body_en: Lucy Bronze delivered an outstanding defensive performance as Chelsea beat Manchester City 1-0 at Stamford Bridge to move above our title rivals and take the top spot in the Women's Super League. Sandy Baltimore's stunning strike on the stroke of half-time proved decisive, but Bronze and her defensive team-mates also played a crucial role in keeping City's dangerous attack at bay. The England international reflected on the challenge of facing City's prolific attacking duo, how the Blues restricted the visitors' threat and the consistency that has taken us to the top of the table. Bronze relished testing herself against the best players in the game, and was particularly pleased with how Chelsea dealt with the threat posed by Lauren Hemp and Khadija Shaw, who have been in fine form for City this season. 'I always say I love playing against top players,' Bronze explained. 'They have two specifically in Lauren Hemp and Khadija Shaw. They are magic for Man City this season, and they can't stop scoring. 'We had to be dogs in this game because we couldn’t give them any chances. We were very focused on that. I think it was Katie McCabe who might have said that! Just be in them and around them, don't let them get any chances, as we know how good they are as players. They just need one chance to score.' Bronze was particularly impressive in her battle with Shaw, using her experience and strength to limit the striker's opportunities and prevent her from getting into dangerous positions inside the penalty area. Lucy continued: 'She's so strong and powerful, that's a big part of her game. You just have to challenge her as best as you can. We restricted her and her movement. She doesn't need much space to turn and shoot, so we restricted her today to just a lot of long balls around the halfway line.' The Chelsea defender also knows Hemp well from their time together with England, with the pair regularly facing each other in training. That familiarity made the contest an enjoyable challenge, although Bronze knew she would need to be fully focused to keep the winger quiet. Lucy continued: 'She's a great player and someone that I play against a lot with England. In training, we're always against each other, at right-back and left-wing, so I love the challenge. I know what a good player she is, how much she challenges me and how much I need to be focused in a game like today. I think I dealt with it pretty well.' The victory lifted Chelsea to the top of the WSL, one point ahead of City, and maintained our unbeaten start to the season in all competitions. Bronze believes that consistency has been a major factor in the team's strong position, even without one prolific goalscorer leading the way. 'We've been consistent all season, but we just haven't been prolific with goals and a main goalscorer,' Lucy added. 'But we've performed well in every game, arguably not against Everton last weekend, but we have been consistent. 'The team has been consistent even when we have changed line-ups, the same in the Champions League as well. We've built a really good group of players who are constantly there and constantly fighting, and we are always ready. Even when making changes in the first half, we just keep going and going.'

news.title: Chizaram Ezenwata on his goalscoring form and hidden talent
news.body_en: At just 18 years old, Chizaram Ezenwata is already making a significant impression at Cobham. The young forward has enjoyed a superb start to the 2026/27 season, finding the net eight times for Harry Hudson’s Cobham Next Gen side and earning a Premier League 2 Player of the Month nomination back in September. Having stepped up to the CNG squad, Ezenwata has quickly adapted to the demands of PL2 football, becoming an increasingly important figure within the squad. His progress is another step in an exciting journey with the Blues, having developed into one of the side's leading attacking threats since joining the club at 15. While his performances on the pitch continue to attract attention, there is more to the young forward than his goalscoring ability. Away from football, Ezenwata recently surprised supporters with a rather different talent, as a video of him playing the piano attracted plenty of attention online. It is an interest he has held since childhood and offers a glimpse into the person behind the footballer. We recently sat down with Ezenwata to discuss his impressive start to the campaign, his development at Cobham, the responsibility of his role within the squad and his ambitions for the remainder of the campaign. 'I can't complain about the start of the season and the eight goals,' Ezenwata explains. 'I’d like it to be higher but that’s just me as a striker. I’ve been playing up with the Under-21s and I feel like I am confident, getting more comfortable and really growing.' One of his standout performances was in the EFL Trophy against Reading in October, when Ezenwata scored a brace in our 2-0 win at the Select Car Leasing Stadium. Aside from his well-taken goals, what was noticeable was the 18-year-old’s strength and ability to hold up play against senior opposition. Ezenwata revealed that this was an area of his game that he has focused on improving further since stepping up to the CNG side. He said: 'I really enjoyed the Reading game; it was a good challenge for me. Obviously, wanting to play first team, having that experience in the EFL Trophy and managing to get two goals, I’m really proud of myself for that. 'I feel like I've adapted to the conditions, obviously with my physical prowess as well. One of my big developing points is my hold-up play; I’ve been working on it more in training, doing the extras. In terms of my finishing, I'm just carrying that on as well.' Despite only turning 18 in September, Ezenwata has become a key figure in our Cobham Next Gen side, taking on the vice-captaincy and leading by example on and off the pitch. He also wore the captain’s armband against Flora Tallinn in the UEFA Youth League first leg, and popped up with a goal in that game. The Blues striker admitted he feels the responsibility but enjoys the role and having his teammates’ trust. He said: 'It means a lot to have this role, so I’m going to keep pushing. From the start of the season to now, you can see the togetherness has grown. We’re all interlinked as one. Playing together more, we just understand each’s abilities and personalities.' Since arriving at Chelsea, Ezenwata has developed rapidly. Last season, he registered 21 goals and nine assists across all competitions, including the opener in our Under-18 Premier League National Final victory against Manchester City at Stamford Bridge to help us seal the title. That followed an impressive 2024/25 campaign in which Ezenwata was a regular starter for the Under-18s and finished as the team’s top scorer. He has since led the line for CNG and recently signed a new contract, keeping him at the club until at least June 2029. Reflecting on the journey with the Blues so far, Ezenwata said: 'Coming to Chelsea when I was fifteen, I was very excited. My family and I were all proud and Chelsea is the world to me now; being full-time, playing week in, week out and enjoying my football. 'Last season’s final against Man City, winning that final, was my proudest moment so far at Chelsea. The emotions at full time were unreal, seeing everyone coming onto the pitch. 'This season, it’s been signing my new deal. It's another step in the right direction and shows my hard work is paying off, so I'm going to keep working hard and strive for more.' Away from football, Ezenwata remains incredibly talented. His skill for playing the piano recently attracted attention online, which surprised the young forward. Ezenwata told us: 'I didn’t expect that many people to be there; you can see at the end of the video when I was looking around. I started playing when I was four years old, teaching myself with YouTube and learning nursery rhymes. I’ve kept doing it ever since - it helps me relax.' The song Ezenwata performed in the video is his favourite to play as it’s the most recent he’s learned and took ‘a while’ to perfect. However, it’s not the most difficult he’s learned, with Drowning Love by Chasing Kou taking top spot. Looking ahead to the remainder of the season, Ezenwata has set himself the target of becoming Premier League 2 top goalscorer and vows to keep working hard to make it happen. He'll have a chance to add to his growing tally at the end of the month when we face Norwich City.

news.title: Chelsea's Player of the Month for October 2026 revealed!
news.body_en: Morgan Rogers' impressive start to life at Stamford Bridge continued in October, with the forward voted Chelsea's Player of the Month by users of the Chelsea Official App. The summer signing featured in all five of our matches during the month, playing 444 of the 450 minutes available across four Premier League fixtures and our Carabao Cup tie. He helped the Blues secure three league victories and enjoyed his most productive month since arriving in West London. Rogers scored three goals during October, two in the Premier League and one in the cup, as he continued to establish himself as a pivotal member of Xabi Alonso's attack. His regular involvement underlined the importance he has quickly gained within the team, with the forward becoming a consistent presence in our starting line-up. His standout moment came against Manchester United at Stamford Bridge, when he opened the scoring with a sensational individual effort. Collecting the ball from Romeo Lavia just inside the centre-circle, the 24-year-old embarked on a powerful run through the heart of the visitors' defence and into the penalty area before delicately lifting his finish over the despairing goalkeeper. It was a goal of exceptional quality and one which was recognised by Blues supporters, with Rogers receiving the Chelsea Goal of the Month award for October. It was the second consecutive month he had claimed that prize, having also been voted September's winner for his volley against Arsenal. The England international's attacking contribution was reflected in his numbers, with ten shots across his five appearances, while he also featured twice for his country during the international break. His willingness to drive forward from midfield and take on opposition defenders has added another dimension to our attacking play, while his ability to operate in different areas of the forward line has made him a valuable option for Alonso. Rogers has made an excellent impression since joining the club in the summer and has already reached ten goal involvements in all competitions this season, underlining the impact he has made in the early stages of his Chelsea career. He finished top of the October Player of the Month poll on the Chelsea Official App with 36 per cent of the vote. Romeo Lavia was second with 30 per cent, followed by Mike Penders on 18 per cent, Pedro Neto on nine per cent and Jordan Henderson on seven per cent.

news.title: Match report: Chelsea Women 1-0 Manchester City
news.body_en: Chelsea moved to the top of the Women's Super League with a huge victory over Manchester City at Stamford Bridge, ending the visitors' unbeaten league record and moving one point clear of them at the summit. Sandy Baltimore's stunning strike in first-half stoppage time proved decisive in a hard-fought contest. The Blues had to withstand considerable pressure after the break, but defended resolutely before City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita was sent off for bringing down Alyssa Thompson outside her penalty area. We remained a threat on the counter and came close to adding a second, but Baltimore's goal was enough to secure three precious points. The result maintains our unbeaten start to the season in all competitions and gives us a significant advantage in the race for the WSL title. The early stages at Stamford Bridge were played at a high tempo, with chances at both ends in an entertaining start to the contest. Manchester City created the first opportunity when Khadija Shaw broke down the left and cut the ball back for Aoba Fujino, whose effort went wide of Hannah Hampton's goal. We responded immediately, with Melvine Malard holding off the City defence before laying the ball into the path of Alyssa Thompson, but the American international fired high and wide. City continued to threaten, but Katie McCabe produced an excellent interception in the eighth minute to prevent Fujino from having another sight of goal. We came close to taking the lead two minutes later. Malard beat Iman Beney down the left and sent in a cross, which took a slight deflection, forcing Ayaka Yamashita into an excellent save. There was an early change for the Blues in the 12th minute, as Veerle Buurman replaced Kadeisha Buchanan in defence. Lexi Potter was shown the first yellow card of the afternoon three minutes later after catching Sam Coffey, before Ellie Carpenter used her pace to get away from the City defence on the right. The Australian drove towards goal but dragged her shot wide of the far post. Our attacking threat continued to grow. McCabe played a superb pass inside the full-back to release Thompson down the left in the 21st minute, and her cross found its way to Carpenter at the far post after Malard had been unable to make contact. Carpenter struck first time, but Rebecca Knaak cleared the ball from inside the six-yard box with Malard waiting to pounce. Baltimore then sent a dangerous cross into the area, which Malard narrowly failed to reach, as City struggled to deal with our attacking play. We were enjoying more possession and creating the better opportunities, although a breakthrough remained elusive. City had a rare effort in the 26th minute when Sydney Wamser tried her luck from around 25 yards, but her shot sailed wide of Hampton's goal. There was an injury concern for us when Malard went down in the 34th minute and, unable to continue, was replaced by Aggie Beever-Jones. The Blues continued to press City and eventually had the final say before the interval. Our pressure was finally rewarded in the fourth minute of added time, as Baltimore produced a stunning finish to put us ahead. City had been caught trying to play out from the back, and we took full advantage by pressing high and winning possession in their half. Buurman won an aerial challenge near halfway before Carpenter held off the City defence and carried the ball forward down the right. City briefly regained possession, but Hasegawa was unable to escape the pressure from Carpenter and Kaptein, who won the ball back. Potter laid it off to Kaptein, who found Carpenter on the right. The full-back then picked out Baltimore inside the penalty area. The French international had time to turn and set herself before unleashing a thunderous strike into the top corner, giving Yamashita no chance and sending Stamford Bridge into delirium. It was a wonderful goal and a deserved reward for our growing dominance. We had looked the more threatening side as the half progressed, shading possession and creating the better chances, and Baltimore's late strike gave us the advantage our first-half performance merited. It was to be Baltimore’s final impact on the game with the attacker replaced by Maika Hamano at the break. City immediately tried to find a way back into the contest after the break, but their first effort on target did not come until the 57th minute when Fujino collected a pass from Shaw. Her tame shot was straight at Hampton, who made a comfortable save. After soaking up the pressure, we continued to threaten at the other end, with McCabe playing a wonderful pass to release Thompson. The forward embarked on a winding run before sending a cross into the area, which was intercepted by the City defence. Our fifth corner followed on the hour mark. McCabe's delivery was cleared, but Bronze returned the ball into the box and Kaptein reacted quickest to the loose ball. Under pressure from Yamashita and Shaw, however, her header went just over the crossbar. The visitors then missed a golden opportunity to equalise. Shaw beat Bronze to the ball before lifting the ball over Hampton, but Hemp somehow failed to make contact at the far post, despite the goal seemingly at her mercy. Carpenter's pressure helped put the England international off, and we survived a major scare. City substitute Miedema soon made her presence felt, playing in Shaw, who cut inside Carpenter before seeing her effort blocked brilliantly by the excellent Buurman. We had a huge opportunity to double our advantage in the 71st minute. Thompson did well to keep the ball alive down the left before sending a cross towards the far post, where Carpenter was completely unmarked. However, the Australian could not make clean contact and fired off target with the goal gaping. City kept on pressing with Fujino skipping past McCabe, but Bronze stepped across to block her effort, before our captain produced another vital intervention to deny Shaw as she prepared to shoot. A decisive moment came in the 75th minute when City goalkeeper Yamashita was sent off. The Japanese international rushed out of her penalty area to meet a ball over the top, but the electric Thompson got there first and knocked it past the onrushing keeper, who brought down our forward. The referee had little choice but to show a straight red card, leaving City with ten players for the closing stages. And we came within inches of making our numerical advantage count immediately; Beever-Jones struck the crossbar from the resulting free-kick, a wonderful effort from distance that was so close to giving us a more comfortable final 15 minutes of action. Despite being down to ten players, City continued to push forward in search of an equaliser, with Bronze continuing to lead our defensive efforts, making another important intervention to prevent Shaw from getting a shot away in the 83rd minute. We remained dangerous on the counter, with Beever-Jones firing wide after a fine run down the left six minutes from time. City had one final opportunity when Beney was played in by Beth Mead in the first minute of added time, but the defender fired over under pressure from the hard-working Thompson. A frenetic, high-quality encounter ended with the Blues claiming all three points to move above City and take the top spot in the WSL. The victory takes us to the top of the Women's Super League, one point ahead of Manchester City, who had been unbeaten in the league and across all competitions before today's meeting. It also extends our own unbeaten start to the season and delivers a significant result against the reigning champions at Stamford Bridge. We host Paris Saint-Germain at the Cherry Red Records Stadium on Wednesday evening (8pm KO) in matchday five of the UEFA Women's Champions League. You can buy your tickets here! news.title: 'Chizzy' Ezenwata on his excellent form for the CNG
Buchanan on togetherness and WSL title focus ahead of Man City visit
news.body_en: Kadeisha Buchanan believes Chelsea have the quality and togetherness to reclaim the Women's Super League title this season – and is determined to help the Blues make a statement against current champions Manchester City this afternoon at Stamford Bridge. We welcome City to SW6 in a contest between the WSL's top two. Only two points separate the teams after nine games, and neither has yet tasted defeat this term. Victory for Sonia Bompastor's side would see us leapfrog City and return to the summit, and Buchanan, who has been part of a Chelsea defence that has conceded just five league goals this term, believes the Blues are ready for the challenge ahead. 'It's at Stamford Bridge, so we're confident,' the Canadian international said. 'I think the last time we played them at Stamford Bridge, we started off defensively strong. And this season, with the stingy back line we have, I think we'll be in a better space. 'If we have that strong start and clean up a few things in defence, I think we'll be very confident in that game.' City arrive in west London boasting an impressive record of their own, with 25 points earned from a possible 27 and Bunny Shaw leading the WSL scoring charts with 12 goals. Buchanan is well aware of the threat posed by the Jamaican forward and believes limiting her opportunities will be crucial to Chelsea's chances of success. 'I think we've got to try to stop the service into Bunny any way possible and be strong physically,' she said. 'I do feel like we've had a good start to this season in both competitions. I think we are in a good space and just hope to keep it like that and improve as the season goes on.' Buchanan also believes our strong start to the campaign has been built on the understanding and togetherness within Bompastor's squad. Seven victories and two draws from our opening nine WSL fixtures have kept us near top spot, and we have also made a strong start to our UEFA Women's Champions League campaign. 'I think the more we work together, the more we move as one,' explained Buchanan.  'It's about team compactness, moving together, knowing our team-mates, knowing how Lucy (Bronze) plays, knowing how Nat (Bjorn) plays, knowing how Veerle (Buurman) plays, knowing how everyone plays on the field so then you can best support them as well.' That collective spirit will be tested against a City side who ended our run of six consecutive WSL titles last season. But while today's opponents represent an obstacle in our pursuit of silverware this term, Buchanan insists the Blues' motivation comes from within rather than from a desire for revenge. 'I can't speak for everyone – it's each to their own – but I don't think it's about them,' she said. 'I think it's about Chelsea and, going off that, I think it's ours to take. 'It [the title] was ours and we lost it. They didn't win it; we lost it. So I feel it's the same this season: it's ours to take if we truly want it, and it's about just not letting it slip this year. 'Win against Man City at home and we're on top. I think after that game, hopefully we get the result we need, we'll be in a really good space.'

news.title: Internationals: Caicedo on target as he leads Ecuador to victory
news.body_en: Moises Caicedo scored Ecuador's second goal as they beat Costa Rica 2-0, with the Chelsea midfielder captaining his country in the victory. The 25-year-old was his usual all-action self in midfield, contributing important defensive work while also getting forward to support Ecuador's attack. His performance was capped in the 83rd minute when he stepped up to take a penalty and put the result beyond doubt. Caicedo struck the ball powerfully and low into the bottom-left corner, giving the Costa Rica goalkeeper no chance, registering his fourth international goal in 66 appearances for Ecuador. The Chelsea midfielder was given the opportunity to rest after his contribution, being substituted immediately after finding the net. His leadership has also been evident at club level this season, with Caicedo having worn the captain's armband for the Blues on several occasions. Chelsea youngster Kendry Paez was also included in the Ecuador squad but did not feature against Costa Rica. Ecuador's next fixture comes on 17 November, when they face Bolivia at 11pm UK time. Meanwhile, none of Chelsea's Argentine trio of Emi Martinez, Valentin Barco and Aaron Anselmino featured in Argentina's 2-1 defeat to Uruguay in an exhibition match. At Under-20 level, Jacob Hall featured for the USA as they took on Japan in Atlanta. The Samurai Blue claimed a 2-0 victory, with both goals already scored by the time Hall was introduced from the substitutes' bench in the 71st minute. The 17-year-old Chelsea academy product was unable to help his side find a way back into the contest. Hall will have another opportunity to impress on international duty in the early hours of Sunday morning, when the USA Under-20s take on Colombia.

news.title: Iconic Chelsea shirts reimagined for Christmas
news.body_en: Chelsea’s new Christmas jumpers have arrived, just in time for the festive party season, so you can show your passion for the Blues and your holiday spirit at the same time. Retro is the theme for Christmas at Stamford Bridge this year, with two of Chelsea’s most iconic kits reimagined in Christmas jumper form, producing the kind of knitwear that will really stand out from the crowd at the office party or family lunch on Christmas Day itself. Shop the full range of Chelsea Christmas jumpers here For Christmas 2026, we are taking things back to the turn of the millennium with a distinctive and ever-popular away shirt from the Nineties, as well as the home kit that kicked off Chelsea’s 21st Century with silverware. Christmas is a time for family, and that was also on people’s minds when Blues skipper Dennis Wise carried his infant son up the famous old Wembley steps to collect the FA Cup trophy after our 1-0 victory over Aston Villa in the 2000 final. It was a truly historic moment, providing one of Chelsea and the FA Cup’s all-time iconic images, as well as being the last time anyone would lift club football’s oldest trophy under the twin towers of the traditional home of the English game, before Wembley was demolished and rebuilt. The shirt our legendary captain Wise was wearing as he did so – one of the most popular retro jerseys still frequently seen in the stands at the Bridge – has now been turned into a Christmas jumper in time for this year’s festivities. There have been a few alterations to add a festive touch, with Christmas-themed messaging replacing the sponsors, while on the back the space reserved for players’ name and number reads ‘Merry 26’, paying tribute to another legendary Blues skipper John Terry, who was taking his early steps in senior football wearing the No26 shirt during the 1999/00 campaign. Our other new Christmas jumper offering mimics the unmistakable away kit worn by Chelsea for the 1994/95 and 1995/96 seasons, instantly recognisable both for its bold design and the era it is associated with. The orange and grey became iconic of a hugely important period in Chelsea’s history, when manager Glenn Hoddle rebuilt the club in his image, being the shirt worn during the debut seasons of global stars like Ruud Gullit, Dan Petrescu and Mark Hughes. Those were the campaigns that laid the groundwork and provided the spark for the most successful spell in Chelsea's history. Of course, those are just two of many Christmas jumpers available from Chelsea, with traditional options also on offer for those who prefer to keep things more festive. news.title: OTD: Chelsea 3-0 Wimbledon | 14 November 1998
Key talking points from Sonia Bompastor's pre-Man City press conference
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor faced the media at Cobham ahead of our huge Women's Super League clash against Manchester City on Saturday, and here are the main talking points from what the Blues head coach said. Bompastor answered the assembled journalists' questions about the game, in which the top two teams in the WSL prepare to face off for the first time this season - with just a couple of points separating the sides. The head coach reported that Lauren James and Naomi Girma will be unavailable until the conclusion of this block of fixtures next weekend, prior to the forthcoming international break. And here are the rest of the key talking points from our head coach’s pre-match press conference on Friday as she looked ahead to a mouthwatering contest. ‘From what you could see from the beginning of the season, probably both teams will want to win the game, and both teams will attack to win the game. ‘Probably you will see goals tomorrow, hopefully for everyone, and not too much for us in terms of conceding! ‘It’s never easy to play teams who are sitting in the low block and not really allowing you to find spaces. I think this game will be different, for sure, in terms of space on the pitch. We need to be smart to recognise that and exploit it.’ ‘The two last results have been frustrating for us, so it's good to see from the players' reaction, but also the staff reaction, that we are hungry. ‘We have hunger going into the game tomorrow. We need to keep working, and I'm convinced we'll create opportunities, and we need to make sure we are clinical. ‘Many things can happen when you are in those moments, and we keep working on the pitch, providing details to the players, reviewing the games, trying to understand what we can do even better to make sure we are able to score in every game.’ ‘She's been really good. She's a player who is able to defend but also to attack, as you could see this season. ‘She’s able to run through that outside corridor. She has improved a lot in terms of the quality of her crossing, but also when she gets in the box, the decision-making on the ball. ‘She's scored some great goals and she's making an impact for us. Even if sometimes people think she can be predictable in what she's doing, she's still really good at doing what she does.’ ‘If we go focus too much on her, another player from Man City will find a way maybe to create and score a goal. We know that because they have a lot of quality as a team, but also they have a lot of great individuals. ‘We believe in the quality of the players we have on the pitch as well. We believe in what we are doing as a team also to defend, especially in the box. We proved that already when we played against Arsenal, when we played against Lyon in the Champions League. ‘We were able to not concede much during those games, we took some learnings, and we'll try to apply the same for the game tomorrow.’ ‘In that game, the mental aspects were the most important ones. When you are leading at home by two goals and you have 15 minutes left in the game, I think you can't let the game go the way it went. ‘But it happens. We took the learnings, and what we know from that game and the quality City has on their side, from minute one until the end of the game they have the opportunity to be a good team and to score at any time. ‘So obviously we know we will have to be a good team from minute one until the end of the game, and make sure we are really switched on.’ See the Blues in action against Man City at Stamford Bridge! news.title: Sonia Bompastor named WSL Manager of the Month
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor has been named Women's Super League Manager of the Month after guiding the Blues to three victories from our three league matches in October. Bompastor's side enjoyed a perfect October in the WSL, netting 12 goals and conceding just three as we maintained our unbeaten start to the campaign. The month began with an impressive 3-0 win away at West Ham United, before the Blues returned to Stamford Bridge following the international break to secure a thrilling 6-2 victory over London rivals Tottenham Hotspur. That derby triumph marked Bompastor's 50th WSL match in charge of Chelsea, with the Blues head coach setting a new WSL record of 125 points from her opening 50 games. In our final league fixture of October, we came from behind to claim a 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace, with Melvine Malard scoring twice in the second half to secure all three points. It is the fifth time Bompastor has received the WSL Manager of the Month award since taking charge in the summer of 2024.

news.title: Bompastor updates on James and Girma availability ahead of Man City
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor confirmed that Lauren James and Naomi Girma are progressing well on their return from injury, but she expects our next match against Manchester City to be too soon for them to be involved. Chelsea face a huge Women’s Super League fixture on Saturday, when we host Manchester City at Stamford Bridge in a top-of-the-table clash. After dropping WSL points for the first time since our opening game of the season, we now sit two points behind leaders Man City, but can retake first place with a home win this weekend. However, the Blues will have to do so without the help of James or Girma, after our manager gave an update on the progress of their recovery from injury. ‘I think LJ is good, but I don’t think we expect to see her in this block,’ said Bompastor, in her pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon. ‘That’s the same for Nay. She’s now more in advance, not far from starting again to train with the team. ‘So both of them are doing good, but we won’t see them in this block with us.’ Even without those two, Bompastor still has plenty of talent at her disposal for this massive WSL fixture, and is confident her team has what it takes to secure what could be a crucial victory in the title race in front of our home support at the Bridge. ‘In terms of that the two teams are unbeaten, it is an important game between two teams that are performing at a really good level, but not the only ones obviously. ‘I think tomorrow it’s a game worth three points, like the other ones, but in terms of the psychological aspects, the team that is able to win will take maybe a psychological advantage. ‘So we are playing at home and we approach every game the same, tomorrow won’t be different. We want to come to the game and bring some confidence, but also try to win the game. I know we have the ability to do that so we will try our best. ‘The game plan is ready. We’ve only had a few training sessions after the Hacken game, but I feel the team is in a good place and ready for the game tomorrow.’ Secure your seat at the Bridge to cheer the team on against Man City! news.title: Mike Penders save voted Premier League’s best
news.body_en: Mike Penders has received the Premier League Save of the Month award for October for his stunning stop against Manchester United. The Blues goalkeeper had competition from five others on the shortlist, but the public vote picked Penders’ save as the best in the Premier League during October. The save which claimed the award came late in our 2-0 win over Manchester United at Stamford Bridge, just one week after the 21-year-old’s full league debut. He showed quick reflexes and excellent agility to divert Bryan Mbeumo’s powerful drive onto the crossbar with his fingertips, keeping his clean sheet intact. It wasn’t just the Premier League supporters casting their vote for the award who were so impressed by the Belgian’s reflexes, as he admitted that even some of his team-mates found it almost too good to believe. ‘The ball came so quickly, I didn’t even see it properly,’ said Penders on his award-winning stop. ‘It was just instinct, pure instinct, a reaction. I felt a good touch on my fingertips and, after that moment, I screamed all the positive emotions out. I had to, I was so happy with that moment. ‘Then, after the game, no-one believed me that I touched it! I was like: “Yeah, I touched it, you will see afterwards”. ‘Then it was pretty quickly on Twitter. A team-mate came into the dressing room saying: “He touched it”. I was very happy it was a good angle, because if the angle wasn't right, they could still have some doubts!’ Penders becomes the third Chelsea goalkeeper to receive the Premier League Save of the Month award since it was introduced for the start of the 2022/23 season, following Kepa Arrizabalaga and Robert Sanchez (twice).

news.title: Cuthbert on heavyweight Man City clash and 'pivotal' fans' support
news.body_en: Erin Cuthbert thinks two of the best sides in women's football will make 'punch after punch' when we face off against Manchester City at Stamford Bridge on Saturday. After winning the Women's Super League last season, Man City head coach Andree Jeglertz has guided them to the top of the table once again this season, but the Blues are chasing hard and sit just two points behind after nine games. Saturday's match couldn't be more finely poised, and when we sat down with our captain Erin Cuthbert, she explained exactly why our fans could be the difference-maker in a match where winning and losing will come down to such fine margins. 'The Stamford Bridge crowd have really excelled in the tough moments this season,' said the skipper. 'There have been times when we've been up against it, but that's when the crowd have got us out of that and swung the momentum back in our favour. 'We’re going to need them against Man City because we're not always going to get it our way. The crowd is going to be really pivotal on Saturday. We feed off their energy. We've needed them at times this season, because it hasn't always been plain sailing, despite how many goals we’ve scored and clean sheets we’ve earned. 'Neither side will play for a point; we’ll both be going for the three points, and hopefully that should see the fans turn out in numbers, because they're going to see a game that both sides want to win right until the very end. 'I expect it to be a very high-quality game, but also to be quite edgy at the same time, because both teams want to win, but both teams don't want to lose. So it's a fine balance between whether you go and risk it all, or hold on to what you've got. I know the team will go for it right until the final whistle, and if we're still in it, we'll be going gung-ho, and if we are winning, we'll fight to keep it that way.' Erin Cuthbert is well used to winning silverware at Chelsea. Joining the club in 2016, she only missed out on our first two trophies, and has lifted 18 since then. The Scotland international was a key member of the side that won six consecutive WSL titles before Man City's success last year, and she's determined to see it back in our hands at the end of the campaign. 'It was our trophy for six years before last season, so of course it feels like it's been taken away,' she explains. 'But Man City were rightful winners last year and beat us comfortably in the end. 'There is a degree of wanting to claim what's ours, because it had been ours for so long, but nobody has any given right to the title. It's built through hard work and grinding out wins, good, bad and ugly, across the season, and we're going to need that. 'We know Man City have it just now, so we have to do everything and more. I've been in the position where we've been top of the table, and we've won the league, so I know what it feels like when teams are chasing you. You feel them breathing down your neck. They're coming for you. You feel that in every game. 'It’s a bit different to be the ones chasing. We're part of the chasing pack now, so it's certainly a different mentality, and you're seeing something maybe a bit different this year: that we're so hungry for it.' Those watching will be in for a treat on Saturday, as the Bridge will showcase the very best of what the WSL has to offer as the top two sides battle it out for the three points. If Man City come out to attack, they could break the trend of visiting sides sitting deep in a low block, and that would give our forwards the space to show what they can do. And although for Cuthbert it is just another opportunity to earn three points, another part of her feels that winning the game will make a big statement about our intentions this season. 'Both teams know the quality each other has got at both ends of the pitch,' the captain continues. 'Man City have a very certain style of play. They're not going to sit back and just take pressure from us all game. They're going to come out fighting, and they have really good technical players who can hurt us, but equally we have those players too. It's going to be punch after punch from both sides. 'Their attacking intent could leave spaces that we might not always have in the league, and it opens up a different type of play for a couple of our players in the team to shine. So it's certainly an exciting one, but also one where we're probably going to be a little bit busier defensively, and we expect that. 'It’s something that the team's ready for, because I think defensively we've done really well this season, and I think big credit goes to the backline and everybody else because the job's been monumental so far.'
